product: Credit reporting or other personal consumer reports
issue: Credit monitoring or identity theft protection services

themes.label: Fraudulent accounts from alleged identity theft
themes.description: Consumers claim identity theft or data breaches led to accounts, charges, or inquiries they did not authorize and seek blocking or removal from credit files.

examples.summary: Consumer claims to be an identity theft victim and requests that credit reporting agencies block and delete fraudulent accounts and associated adverse information from their credit reports in compliance with Fair Credit Reporting Act Section 605B requirements.
Consumer claims to have received letters from a credit card company for an account they did not open, with $1,000 in fraudulent charges, and reported the matter to the credit bureau.
Consumer claims a furnisher failed to remove a fraudulent account from credit reports despite submission of an FTC identity theft report and proper dispute documentation.

themes.label: Disputed credit report errors not corrected
themes.description: Consumers allege inaccurate or previously disputed items remain or reappear on credit reports despite disputes, documentation, or reinvestigation requests.

examples.summary: Consumer disputes the accuracy of account information being reported to credit reporting agencies and demands verification and cessation of reporting.
Consumer alleges a credit reporting entity furnished inaccurate late payment information while an account was in deferment and failed to correct errors after being notified of disputes.

Consumer claims disputed negative items on credit reports from two bureaus reappeared after initial disputes and that furnishers provided no validation information despite requests, resulting in significant credit score damage and inability to obtain credit.

themes.label: Unexplained charges and unfamiliar accounts reported
themes.description: Consumers claim unrecognized charges, services, or collection accounts appeared on their credit reports or bills without their request, sometimes followed by debt sales.

examples.summary: Consumer claims a company charged them for a credit monitoring or identity theft protection service that was placed on their bill without authorization or their having obtained the service.
Consumer claims a collection account appeared on their credit report for a service they did not receive and did not request.
Consumer claims a delinquent account from an unfamiliar creditor appeared on their credit report without authorization.

themes.label: Credit monitoring service access and support failures
themes.description: Consumers report being unable to access or use credit monitoring or identity protection services, or not receiving promised support.

examples.summary: Consumer claims they are unable to dispute items on their credit report, remove fraud alerts and credit freezes, or view their credit score due to repeated error messages on their credit monitoring account.
Consumer claims they were unable to access complimentary credit monitoring service following a data breach and received ineffective support from customer service.

Consumer alleges failure to provide promised identity theft protection services and specialist assistance, account access restrictions, inadequate departmental coordination, and unauthorized sharing of personal information with debt collectors and international third parties.

themes.label: Payment handling issues causing late reporting
themes.description: Consumers allege stopped automatic payments or undisclosed account freezes led to missed payments and negative credit reporting.

examples.summary: A credit card company allegedly stopped automatic payments without notification or consumer consent, resulting in a late payment being reported to credit bureaus and a significant credit score decrease.
Consumer claims bank froze account without adequate disclosure, preventing timely mortgage and other payments, resulting in delinquency reporting and derogatory credit marks.

brief.headline: Identity theft and uncorrected dispute claims persist in credit reporting complaints, with bank over-representation
brief.what_is_happening: Complaints in this credit reporting and credit monitoring cluster are roughly steady with a slight uptick. The recent monthly average is 640.0 against a baseline of 605.83 (velocity 1.0559, rank 19 of 79), and August 2026 reached 770 complaints. In a sample of 38 AI-reviewed narratives, the main themes are claimed identity theft leading to fraudulent accounts (37.8%), disputed errors that allegedly were not corrected (27.0%), and unexplained charges or unfamiliar accounts (21.6%). Smaller themes are credit monitoring access and support failures (8.1%) and payment handling issues causing late reporting (5.4%). These are unverified allegations.
brief.who_is_affected: Consumers who claim identity theft or inaccurate or unrecognized items on their credit files. The AI sample estimates 18.4% are vulnerable consumers, and mean severity is 3.68 out of 5. Complaints concentrate in TX (13.9%), FL (11.5%), CA (10.7%) and LA (10.7%). Large banks and card issuers appear far above their expected share within this product, while the three major credit bureaus have lift below 1.
brief.likely_root_cause: Hypothesis to test: weak handoffs between furnishers (banks and card issuers) and credit bureaus when identity theft claims or disputes are filed. Fraud determinations may not flow into credit reporting corrections, and blocked or disputed items may be reinserted or re-reported. A second hypothesis is that credit monitoring or identity protection add-on enrollment and billing may not be adequately authorized. The sample is small and these are alleged causes only.
brief.process_or_control_to_check: Furnisher dispute and identity theft block handling: how fraud case outcomes are communicated to credit reporting data furnishing teams, how reinvestigation requests are processed, and how re-reporting of previously disputed items is prevented. Also review enrollment authorization and billing controls for credit monitoring or identity protection add-on products, and the handling of stopped automatic payments that lead to late payment reporting.
brief.regulatory_area: Credit reporting accuracy and dispute handling, including identity theft related blocking of information, plus consumer authorization for ancillary financial products
evidence: Recent monthly average of 640.0 complaints versus a baseline monthly average of 605.83 (velocity 1.0559, rank 19 of 79)

checks.name: size
checks.reason: The brief's bank over-representation claim is supported by lifts of 11.5 to 18.0 for Capital One, Bank of America, JPMorgan Chase, Citibank, Synchrony and Wells Fargo, while the bureaus sit below 1 (0.675 to 0.948), so company size does not explain it.

checks.name: templating
checks.reason: The templated share of recent narratives is 0.0%, well under the 30% threshold.

checks.name: concentration
checks.reason: The top state, TX, holds only 13.9% of complaints, with FL, CA and LA at 10.7% to 11.5%, and the complaints span many companies, so no single state or company drives it.

checks.name: thin_evidence
checks.reason: Only 9 narratives exist in the recent months, below the minimum of 10, even though the 38-complaint sample is adequate and its identity-theft and dispute themes cover about 65% of it.

checks.name: seasonality
checks.reason: The recent average of 640 depends on August's 770 spike (June 603, July 547); without August the average is about 575, below the 605.83 baseline, so the rise rests on one peak month.

skeptic.note: Rejected because only 9 recent narratives back the root cause and the modest uptick (velocity 1.06) rests entirely on a single August spike.
